this one, so a model added here costs one pass of the matrix, not one pass
per optimizer iteration — that coupling was COS-14.
Measured cost per baseline cell on the five shared cases: haiku $0.0232,
sonnet $0.1013, opus $0.1493, fable $0.2345 — and a mean $0.9681 on a
write-then-verify agentic case, where the worst single cell ran $1.1315.
Budget off the worst cell, not the mean: these are the priciest cells here.
Fable has no bare alias. Measure the top tier by passing its full SDK id:
Quote the id: the [1m] is a glob pattern in zsh. And name --variants —
omitting it runs all five, which is 5x the cells you meant.
//variants: Each variant is a harness-level configuration tested independently of the
style text, so you can tell whether a failure comes from the style wording
or from how Claude Code injects it.

variants.note: Exactly what a user gets today: style file + outputStyle setting, nothing else.
Force Claude Code's long system prompt. Opus gets an abridged one by default; the long one carries explicit anti-verbosity rules.
Anthropic's Opus 5 guidance: in a long system prompt, repeat a one-line version of the length rule near the end.
variants.tailReminder: Keep outputs short and dense. Lead with the outcome. No filler, no emoji, no process narration.

variants.note: Restate the contract in CLAUDE.md, which Claude Code wraps in an explicit override directive and re-injects as a user message.
variants.claudeMd:
# Response style

The active output style is binding. Every reply must obey it:

- Lead with the outcome in the first sentence.
- Sentences under 20 words. No filler, no emoji, no celebration.
- Do not narrate process. Report findings and results only.
- Status updates answer: what I did / did it work / what you do next.

variants.note: Long prompt + tail reminder + CLAUDE.md together.

//improve: models is this loop's own list and is not the matrix's. It is billed once
per candidate per iteration, so it multiplies: 3 models x 6 iterations is
18 measured arms before the reserve gate. Adding a tier here is a much
larger commitment than adding one to the top-level models. Omitting the key
warns and falls back to the cheapest tier alone; --models overrides it.
trainSplit and holdoutSplit are the loop's own signals. reserveSplit is not:
the loop never selects it, and it is measured once at the end to validate the
candidate the loop wants to adopt. minReserveDelta is deliberately as tight as
minHoldoutDelta even though it sits inside the noise floor — rejecting a sound
rewrite costs a re-run, adopting a bad one ships a regression.
